entries.question: 5. If A = {x : x = n², n ∈ W and n < 4}, B = {x : x = n², n ∈ N and n ≤ 4} and C = {0, 1, 2, 5, 6}, then verify the associative property of intersection of sets.
entries.sourceTranscriptionStatus: provisional — C roster and squared-expression typesetting require page-image comparison
steps: The whole numbers n less than 4 are 0, 1, 2, 3. Squaring gives A = {0, 1, 4, 9}.
The natural numbers n at most 4 are 1, 2, 3, 4. Squaring gives B = {1, 4, 9, 16}.
Compute A ∩ B = {1, 4, 9}. Then (A ∩ B) ∩ C = {1}, since only 1 also belongs to C.
Compute B ∩ C = {1}. Then A ∩ (B ∩ C) = {1}.
The two sides are identical: (A ∩ B) ∩ C = A ∩ (B ∩ C) = {1}. This verifies associativity of intersection for these sets.
